title: Planck's baseline column gives a universe age of 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr
summary: Table 2's baseline column, TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing, lists the age as 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr. The conclusions round the present day to 13.8 billion years.
body: In Planck 2018 results VI, Table 2 lists base-ΛCDM parameters. The caption says the baseline results are Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing. In that column the age is 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr, a 68 percent interval. Table 1's Plik column for the same baseline fit prints the same 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr. The conclusions describe the model as reaching the present day at an age of 13.8 billion years, which is that figure rounded. Table 1's caption says a total systematic uncertainty of around 0.5 σ may be more realistic than the quoted statistical error alone, and that values should not be overinterpreted past that. The age is a derived parameter of this fit, not a stopwatch reading. Other columns of Table 2 print other ages. This card uses the baseline column the caption names.
